The abdominal X-ray confirms a distal obstruction with dilated bowel loops and no gas in the rectum. Since the infant has not passed meconium, has there been any blood in the stool or "currant jelly" discharge?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound shows normal readings, which is reassuring regarding structural anomalies like malrotation with volvulus. To further evaluate for Hirschsprung's disease, has the infant shown any signs of delayed passage of stool beyond 48 hours of life?

REQUEST TEST: Anorectal_Manometry

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (Congenital Aganglionic Megacolon)

The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, failure to pass meconium, and the X-ray findings of a distal obstruction are classic for this condition. The normal anorectal manometry supports the absence of reflex relaxation seen in normal infants. I recommend a definitive rectal suction biopsy to confirm the diagnosis histologically.
